result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A gives a more balanced view of whether variable fonts are better: it says when they help, when they make no difference, and when they can be worse. It also gives fuller next steps, including whose name the licence is in, visitor limits and setting a fallback font. Its line 'Your designer chose it, so it's fine to use' sits just before the licensing section and could be misread as permission to use the font online, which is a small flaw. Answer B is clear and usefully offers to read the licence details stored inside the file, but its 'Usually, yes' leans toward overselling; neither answer mentions system fonts as an alternative. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B is more balanced on whether a variable font is better: it says plainly when one makes no difference or can be worse, while A opens with 'Usually, yes.' B also gives more useful licence questions, such as whose name the licence is in and whether it covers web embedding, plus a safe fallback. B's line 'Your designer chose it, so it's fine to use' is a small flaw because it could be read as clearing the licence question. A's offer to read the licence details built into the font file is a nice touch.
